These are the program rules for Everyday Points, the rewards program of Example Bank credit cards, including the Everyday Visa.

Dining credit: up to $10 in statement credits each month when you pay with your card at Example Eats. Enrollment required. Credits post within two billing cycles and unused amounts don't roll over.

1. Earning points

You earn points on eligible purchases, less returns and other credits. Eligible purchases don't include balance transfers, cash advances, travelers checks, gift cards sold by your bank, purchases of foreign currency, interest charges, fees or unauthorized charges.

The category a purchase falls in depends on the merchant category code the merchant chose. We don't decide which category a merchant is in, and we can't change it. Purchases through third-party payment accounts or at merchants located inside another store may not earn bonus points.

2. Redeeming points

You can redeem points for a statement credit, a deposit into an eligible bank account, gift cards or travel. The value of a point depends on how you redeem it. Points have no cash value except as described in these rules.

We may change these rules, including how you earn and redeem points, at any time. If we make a change that's unfavorable to you, we'll tell you in advance as the law requires. Points can be forfeited if your account is closed for fraud or abuse.

3. Other terms

Points aren't your property and can't be transferred except as these rules allow. Taxes on rewards, if any, are your responsibility. Example Bank is a fictional bank used only in software tests; nothing here describes a real program.
